rationale: W0 for n-dodecane (a fuel of the Cool Flames Investigation, PSI-39), one shot for this fuel and not zero-shot: no n-dodecane outcome was opened, but the law is the n-heptane law of flex_heptane.wsp5, whose numbers were typed after the n-heptane train partition. Each fuel-specific number is the n-heptane number times a ratio worked by hand from property values: the hot-flame level, its oxygen and pressure dependence and the heat-up from a transfer number that includes the heating of the liquid; the critical diameter of radiative extinction as the inverse of the mass burning flux; the cool-flame rate from the wet-bulb transfer number under a 700 K flame and its end diameter from an equal residence time; the unlit droplet as self-cooling evaporation with property constants. Heating the liquid to its boiling point costs twice the latent heat, so the hot flame of a large droplet burns slowly over a surface far below boiling, no faster than the cool flame that follows. The oxygen limit of the cool flame (0.03 atm) is a judgement under a published bound for n-decane; the proportionality of the cool-flame end diameter to the initial diameter is extrapolated from n-heptane droplets of 2.4-4.2 mm to 3.8-6.5 mm. The forward has no reignition of the hot flame, no separate warm-flame stage, no direct cool ignition and no fibre, refuses above 4.4 atm and stops 45 s after ignition. The prefix is trusted more and every spread is wider than for n-heptane. Literal revision of the fuel's lineage root (the D^2-law reference of n-heptane, copied without change), not a root, because the author has seen other candidates; it writes every authored element, so nothing of the root survives. The parent id is a placeholder until the fuel is registered in droplet6.rs and the root is built: tools/wsp/reassemble.py then writes it. See docs/wsp/research/phys_droplet_fuels.md.
